Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra, Don Quixote, translated by John Ormsby.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/miguel-de-cervantes-saavedra/don-quixote/john-ormsby

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra, author, writer of the preface, died 1616.
- John Ormsby, translator, writer of the preface, died 1895.

First publication of the text used: 1885 (SE colophon: 'Don Quixote was published in 1605 and 1615 by Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra. It was translated from Spanish in 1885 by John Ormsby.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1885, before 1931, so it is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin: every person named above died in 1925 or earlier (the last to die did so in 1895). So the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less, whatever its country of first publication.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
